correctness.rationale: The mass-normalized Jacobi matrix is irreducible for every positive spring vector, guaranteeing simplicity and smooth eigenvalue branches. The normalized Hellmann–Feynman identity gives each coupling derivative as the square of the corresponding bond extension. Simultaneous vanishing forces every external bond unstretched; all nonzero dimer optical equations then imply identical isolated optical squared frequencies, and propagation excludes a zero dimer. Conversely the explicit nonzero recurrence solves every internal optical pair while nulling each external force for arbitrary couplings. Exactly N internal sign changes and no external sign changes force ordinal N+1 by Sturm oscillation. The packaged checker independently assembled all full finite mass/stiffness matrices and passed 5,500 categorized tests; analytic proof, not finite sampling, establishes universal scope. No convergence or exhaustion assumption is needed.

value.rationale: A natural design question is when a finite mechanical lattice can carry one exactly frequency-fixed vibration despite arbitrarily strong and independent changes in the springs connecting its cells. The answer is a sharp necessary-and-sufficient condition on local isolated optical frequencies, an exact index guaranteeing the branch cannot exchange order, and a recurrence providing programmable localization in nonuniform materials. Unlike perturbative flatness, the mode profile is invariant throughout an open full-dimensional positive coupling cone; all first-order flat points have this global rigidity. This is a structurally motivated robust-frequency classification, not a numerical table, textbook substitution, or generic topological claim.
